title: Old Plastic Could Become Engine Oil
summary:
Old pipes, window frames, and credit cards might one day help make engine oil.

Scientists at Virginia Tech found a new way to turn PVC, a very hard plastic to recycle, into a key part of man-made engine oil.

Chemist Guoliang (Greg) Liu led the team. They turned PVC into polyalphaolefin, a material used to make engine oil and other lubricants. The study was published in the journal Nature.

PVC is hard to recycle because it contains chlorine and many added chemicals. Those chemicals make recycling tricky. So most old PVC ends up buried in landfills.

Meanwhile, demand for engine oil is growing, and making it can harm the environment. Engine oil cuts friction between moving parts, helping engines run well and last longer.

To make the new oil, the team puts PVC in a liquid, adds two chemicals, and heats the mix to 158 degrees Fahrenheit for three hours. Then they collect a thick oil.

'We have proved that it is feasible to use plastic waste to make high-performance lubricants,' Liu said.

Earlier, Liu's lab turned other old plastic into soap ingredients.
why_it_matters: Old pipes, window frames, and credit cards from your home could one day be turned into useful engine oil instead of being buried as trash.
